newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gems of Lebanese divorcee net $12 million.
newsitem.headline: Gems of Lebanese divorcee net $12 million.

text.p: More than 140 designer jewels being sold by a Lebanese divorcee netted 15.1 million swiss francs ($12.1 million), exceeding estimates, Christie's auction house said on Tuesday.

Part of the proceeds from the fabulous collection, owned by Mouna al-Ayoub, the former wife of Saudi businessman Nasser Al-Rachid, will go to eight medical institutes and charity foundations in Europe, Lebanon and the United States, it added.
Francois Curiel, director of Christie's international jewellery department who conducted the auction, announced at the end: "The sale was 100 per cent. Every lot found a buyer."

The star lot, a suite of diamond jewellery by the Lebanese jeweller Tabbah, went for 1.9 million swiss francs ($1.5 million) to a New York bidder in the room. It comprised a choker necklace, matching pendant and ear pendants.

A Bulgari three-row gold beaded necklace, matching bracelet and pair of earrings -- worn by Sharon Stone in the film "Casino" -- went for more than triple the pre-sale estimate, bringing in nearly 60,000 swiss francs ($50,000).

Mouna al-Ayoub, 39-year old mother of five who lives in Paris, was believed to be in Saudi Arabia during the sale, visiting her children. However, she viewed her gems on display in Geneva over the weekend, Christie's said.
